Target: D_B(T_k) = k^2 - k for all k >= 1, both bounds, with explicit extremal gamma_k = (k-1,k-1,k-2,...,2,1,1). Checked step by step.

Part I. Lemma 1 (cell rule): the column-by-column image computation is correct for all three rules, including the boundary columns 1, q+1 and c >= q+2; injectivity follows from disjoint contiguous height ranges. Consequence (a) (diagonal rotation when lambda_1 <= s+1, holes included) and (b) (potential W non-increasing, strict iff a type-3 cell exists) are read off correctly. Lemma 2: the claim 'mu != delta_k implies a diagonal w with a hole and a cell on diagonal w+1' is correct (the case 'diagonals 1..D-1 full' forces T_{D-1} < |mu| <= T_D hence D = k and diagonal k full). The CRT argument (gcd(w,w+1)=1) puts the hole at (w,1) and the cell at (1,w+1) simultaneously, giving lambda_1 >= w+1 >= s+2, contradicting the no-type-3 regime after m_0. Uniqueness of the cyclic partition follows. Hence d_B(lambda) = min{m : B^m(lambda) = delta_k}, which Part III uses.

Part II (lower bound). The family S(p_H,p_X) is correctly characterised (partition iff p_X != p_H, p_H+1; heights and column counts as stated). The only member with a type-3 cell is S(k,1) = (k+1,k-1,...,2), and B(S(k,1)) = delta_k is verified directly. Elsewhere the rotation gives p_H -> p_H+1 mod k, p_X -> p_X+1 mod (k+1). Starting at gamma_k = S(1,k+1), the first time hitting (k,1) is t_0 with t_0 = k-1 mod k, t_0 = 1 mod k+1: a = k-2 mod (k+1) is correct, t_0 = k^2-k-1, so d_B(gamma_k) = k^2-k. Checked k=2: (1,1,1) -> (3) -> (2,1). Correct.

Part III (upper bound, Griggs-Ho method, fully re-proved). Lemma 3 (bookkeeping) and (3.1)/(3.2) are correct. Lemma 4: delta_i = c_i + 1 - c_{i+1} equals the number of 1-parts, expressed as a sum of 0/1 summands; the two 'persistence' consequences follow. Lemma 5 (sandwich) is correct. Lemma 6(1): c_t = k-1 via the argument that c_t = k would force mu = delta_k; (2): the largest i in [t-k,t-2] with e_{t,i}=0 gives (6.1); Case A yields (ii) by sandwich; Case B yields (i) or (ii) by sandwich, and the residual case is killed by the exact card count |B^{t-1}(lambda)| <= 2 + sum_{u=3}^{k} u = T_k - 1 (I verified the part sizes c_j - (t-1-j) <= m+1 and the range of j; the k=2 degenerate case is also consistent). Lemma 7: the unique extra one in row p+k; the case j >= 2 is excluded using delta_{p+k-1}=0, delta_{p+k-2}=1 with the unique death of P_p (needs k >= 3, correctly assumed), yielding c_j >= c_{j-1}+2, contradiction; so c_1 >= p+k-1 and p+k <= n+1. Lemma 8 and Lemma 9 are correct; in Lemma 9 the induction claim, the non-emptiness of U (via delta_{q-1}=0 giving c_{p'+M} >= y+1), and m* >= 2 from (9.2) all check out, producing a y-pattern with y <= x, p' >= p-x, length in [2, q-p-1]. Lemma 10 iterates correctly: p <= x + (q-p-2)x = x(q-p-1). Theorem B: k=1,2 by hand; k >= 3: Case 1 (pattern of length k in (ii)) forces p = t-k+1, q = t+1 and Lemma 7 gives t <= T_k <= k^2-k (valid for k >= 3); Case 2 has length <= k-1 and Lemma 10 gives p <= k(k-2), whence t <= p+k <= k^2-k in (i) and t <= p+k-1 in (ii). All quantifiers/boundary indices (p >= 1 since t-k >= 1; j_0 < i in Lemma 4 applications) are respected.

The external source (Griggs-Ho Thm 3.7) is used only as a method; nothing is cited as a black box, so no conditional dependency remains. The computational artifacts are sanity checks only and are not relied upon. Both bounds are established; the exact formula k^2-k and the extremal partition are given explicitly as functions of k.
